post.quote: Do what you can, with what you've got, where you are.
post.author: Bill Widener
post.source_detail: Theodore Roosevelt: An Autobiography (1913), Chapter IX, 'Outdoors and Indoors'. Roosevelt introduces it as 'a bit of homely philosophy, quoted by Squire Bill Widener, of Widener's Valley, Virginia'.
post.practice: List what you have right now: time, tools, people. Pick one action you can take with it today, without waiting for more.
post.question: What can you do today with what you have?
post.machine_matched: wording matched to Project Gutenberg #3335. Often misattributed to Roosevelt directly; he credits Widener. Decide how you want it credited

caption:
Doers start before they feel ready.

“Do what you can, with what you've got, where you are.”
— Bill Widener, quoted in T. Roosevelt's Autobiography

Try this today: List what you have right now: time, tools, people. Pick one action you can take with it today, without waiting for more.

What can you do today with what you have? Tell me in the comments.

Save this in your journal, or share it with a trusted advisor or accountability partner who will keep you moving.
